The Panel's Take
Google Scion is an experimental open-source multi-agent orchestration testbed from Google Cloud Platform that runs each AI coding agent in its own isolated container with separate credentials and git worktrees.
It supports Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex under one orchestration layer across Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes, providing a vendor-neutral "hypervisor for agents."
The architecture treats agents as isolated processes — each agent can only see its own environment, preventing cross-contamination of secrets, code, or context.
A top-level orchestrator assigns tasks, routes outputs, and mediates agent-to-agent communication through well-defined message-passing interfaces rather than shared memory.
Released April 7-8, 2026, Scion gained 1,000+ GitHub stars immediately.
What's unusual is that Google explicitly built it to support their competitors' agent runtimes — Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex sit alongside Gemini CLI as first-class supported agents.
The research-first, production-later positioning and the puzzle-solving demo suggest this is as much a safety/reliability research tool as a deployment platform.

Agents that share the project workspace see the project’s `.scion` directory read-only, so they cannot edit `.scion/templates/<name>` in place.
Edit the template in another directory of the checkout and sync it by path, for example `scion templates sync ./templates/planner --name planner`.
`sync` is content-aware: it hashes files and uploads only what changed, and templates carry a content hash for traceability (visible in `scion templates list`, `scion templates show`, and the Web UI).
Syncing an existing template mirrors the local directory: files deleted locally are removed from the Hub copy, and sync lists them as it removes them.
On the Hub, a template’s files are stored as content-addressed blobs, and each commit swaps the template’s file manifest in one compare-and-swap step.

**Review workflow:**

> - **Review loops**: `signal_done → submit_feedback → fix → re-review → approve`

> Every agent slot has a `task_state` that governs the review/approval workflow:

> - **idle → working**: Auto-transitions when agent calls `set_summary` or produces first output
> - **working → done_pending_review**: Agent calls `signal_done`
> - **working → approved**: Reviewer/QA agents auto-approve on `signal_done` (they don't need external review)
> - **done_pending_review → addressing_feedback**: Reviewer calls `submit_feedback(actionable=true)`
>
> - **addressing_feedback → done_pending_review**: Agent fixes issues and calls `signal_done` again
> - **done_pending_review → approved**: Reviewer calls `approve`
> - **approved → released**: Orchestrator calls `release_agent`
>
> Agents **cannot disconnect** until explicitly released. This ensures the review loop completes.

# What agent combinations are you running? #14
## OscarDoh Sep 20, 2026
We built Sno Station for Claude Code and Codex.
That's the combo we use every day.
One does the heavy thinking, the other picks up the parallel stuff and reviews.
It works.
Most of the time.

results.snippet: # Dan Kornas on X: "Running several AI agents shouldn’t mean manually moving context between them. Sno Station is an open-source workstation for builders who want coding and general-purpose agents to work as one local squad. It helps you keep work moving between agents by giving them shared encrypted memory, agent-to-agent handoffs, and cross-harness review workflows on your own machine. Key features: • Shared encrypted memory – Codex, Claude Code, Hermes Agent, Cursor, and OpenClaw can use one workspace on your machine • Agent handoffs – when one agent hits its cap, another can pick up the task from shared memory and the mailbox • Cross-harness review – ask one agent to peer-review work from another harness • Approval-gated nightly loop – it reads sessions and proposes skill changes that you accept or reject • Local-first setup – no daemon, server, or cloud is required; the cloud side is optional It’s open-source (Apache License 2.0). Link in the reply 👇"
